passage:
Note, Tuesday session, fest planning group. I sat at the back as agreed. Imran answered nearly every idea with "That will never work." Jaya offered a silent-disco stall and got that reply; the next suggestion, a rooftop film night, got it too. By the fifth idea the room had gone quiet. The list on the board ended up as a chai stall, a quiz and tug-of-war, all things done last year. Jaya stopped looking up from the phone. Afterwards I spoke with Imran alone and asked what he was trying to protect. He said he did not want the fest to flop. I suggested holding all judging back for a second round next week, and I will open the session with that rule.

Faculty advisor

qa.q: Which three ideas ended up on the board?
qa.a: The board ended up with a chai stall, a quiz and tug-of-war.

qa.q: What was Imran worried about, according to what he told the advisor?
qa.a: Imran was worried that the fest would flop, which explains why he shot down each idea.

qa.q: What went wrong in the session, and what could fix it?
qa.a: Judging every idea as it was spoken made people stop offering them, so only safe ones were left. Collecting ideas first and judging later, as the advisor plans for next week, could fix it.

qa.q: How might Jaya have felt after the silent-disco stall was dismissed?
qa.a: Jaya probably felt discouraged and a bit embarrassed, which fits with looking down at the phone and going quiet.

grounding: Shows constant criticism during a brainstorm silencing the group so only familiar ideas reach the list.

passage:
Wednesday night
Today's fest brainstorm was a disaster and I think it was partly me.
We had one hour to plan the college cultural night. Pema started: "What about a silent disco?" I said, "Where will we get headphones? Never works." Then someone said a food-truck lane. I said, "The principal will never allow it." Someone said an open-mic poetry night. Arjun laughed and said, "Who'll come to that?"
After about fifteen minutes, nobody was saying anything. People were just looking at their phones.
In the end the list said: dance competition, DJ night, food stalls. Exactly what we did last year and the year before.
Pema didn't speak again for the whole meeting. On the way out she said, "Next time I'll just send my ideas on chat."
I think I killed the good ones before they could grow.
Chinmay

qa.q: What three items ended up on the list?
qa.a: Dance competition, DJ night, food stalls.

qa.q: How is Chinmay feeling while writing the diary?
qa.a: Chinmay feels guilty and regretful, thinking the good ideas were killed before they could grow.

qa.q: What would you change first in how the brainstorm was run?
qa.a: Agree to a no-judging round first, where every idea is written down, and only after that discuss what is practical.

qa.q: How did Pema experience the meeting?
qa.a: Pema felt shut down after the first idea was dismissed, stayed silent for the rest of the meeting and decided to share ideas on chat instead.

grounding: It shows a college brainstorm where each idea is criticised as soon as it is spoken, so people go quiet and only safe, familiar suggestions are listed.
